caption_fb:
Ellis Island didn't change your family's name.

Passenger lists were written in Europe, when the ticket was bought. Officers in New York checked names against that list. They didn't write new ones. Changes came later, in America: at work, at school, at naturalization.

What it means for your search:
🔹 Look for the Polish spelling on the passenger list (Wiśniewski, not Wisnesky)
🔹 Try spellings a clerk might hear: W/V, SZ/SH, CZ/CH
🔹 Search the first name in Polish too: Stanisław, not Stanley

Your family story didn't start in America.
